skill.name: prisma-compute
skill.description: Guides Prisma Compute configuration, deployment, framework readiness, environment setup, operational checks, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Deploy and troubleshoot TypeScript applications on Prisma Compute.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malicious collection endpoint was found; most static matches are Markdown or deployment documentation. The skill still handles secret-bearing environment files, executes mutable package versions, and documents non-interactive production mutations.

remediation.issue: Package-runner commands use mutable latest tags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions and verify package provenance before bunx, npx, or pnpm dlx execution.

remediation.issue: Deployment examples read and upload secret-bearing environment files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before each environment upload, show variable names only, and verify project, branch, and role scope.

remediation.issue: Some examples permit database URLs in command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer protected environment files, standard input, or platform secret APIs so credentials do not enter shell history or process listings.

remediation.issue: Production and destructive commands use non-interactive confirmation flags.
remediation.suggestion: Request fresh confirmation for the exact target and action, then default deployments to an unpromoted candidate for verification.

content.value_statement: Prisma Compute deployments require correct framework, environment, and authentication settings. This skill guides configuration, deployment, verification, and troubleshooting across supported TypeScript frameworks.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates Compute readiness for Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, Hono, NestJS, TanStack Start, Bun, and custom artifacts.
Creates or updates typed Compute configuration for single applications, monorepos, ports, entrypoints, build output, and environment inputs.
Selects CLI flows for scaffolding, building, deploying, promoting, rolling back, logging, domains, branches, and project environment variables.
Diagnoses authentication, workspace, build artifact, branch scope, database, environment, host binding, port, and public ingress failures.
Explains Compute SDK and Management API patterns for authenticated automation and prebuilt artifact deployment.
limitations: It does not provide credentials, database URLs, workspace access, or deployment authorization.
It cannot guarantee current CLI behavior without checking installed command help and project files.
It does not replace framework tests, database migrations, observability, or production change controls.
SvelteKit requires a custom or prebuilt server artifact because no direct Svelte deployment key exists.

use_cases.title: Prepare Framework Deployment
use_cases.description: Check a Hono, NestJS, or Bun application for correct entrypoint, host, port, and environment settings.

use_cases.title: Operate Preview and Production Releases
use_cases.description: Select projects, branches, environment roles, deployment targets, verification steps, promotion, and rollback commands.

use_cases.title: Build Platform Automation
use_cases.description: Use Compute SDK and Management API guidance to design authenticated deployment tooling with redacted outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Check Deployment Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Prisma project for Compute readiness. Identify its framework, entrypoint, port, host binding, environment source, and safest next step.

prompt_templates.title: Create Compute Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create or update prisma.compute.ts for this application. Preserve existing behavior, avoid secret values, and explain each deployment default.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failed Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Troubleshoot this failed Prisma Compute deployment. Inspect build output, authentication context, branch scope, logs, host binding, and port configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Design Monorepo Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a non-interactive deployment workflow for this monorepo. Include target selection, preview isolation, secret handling, verification, promotion, rollback, and failure reporting.

output_examples.input: Check my Hono API before deploying to Compute.
output_examples.output: Readiness report: Hono target detected. Verify the server entrypoint, all-interface binding, deployed port, environment source, and authentication context before deployment.

output_examples.input: My production deployment succeeded, but its public URL times out.
output_examples.output: Troubleshooting result: inspect runtime logs, compare configured and listening ports, and confirm the server is not bound only to loopback.

output_examples.input: Plan preview deployments for the web and API packages in my monorepo.
output_examples.output: Delivery plan: define separate targets, align branch-scoped environments, build each artifact, deploy unpromoted candidates, verify public endpoints, then promote approved releases.

best_practices: Inspect existing scripts, configuration, framework output, and CLI help before changing deployment behavior.
Confirm workspace, project, branch, environment role, and production intent before any remote mutation.
Redact tokens, database URLs, environment values, and signed upload links from logs and summaries.
anti_patterns: Do not use placeholder database URLs or commit secret values into Compute configuration.
Do not deploy production changes with confirmation bypasses unless the user explicitly approves the exact target.
Do not treat local readiness or build success as proof that public ingress works.

faq.question: Is prisma.compute.ts required?
faq.answer: No. Simple applications can use explicit CLI flags, while reusable defaults and monorepos benefit from a Compute configuration file.

faq.question: Which frameworks have direct deployment support?
faq.answer: Supported keys include Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, Hono, NestJS, TanStack Start, Bun, and custom artifacts.

faq.question: How does the skill authenticate?
faq.answer: It uses existing OAuth sessions or service-token environment variables. It verifies context without printing secret values.

faq.question: Can it deploy directly to production?
faq.answer: Yes, after explicit production intent. Safer workflows build an unpromoted candidate, verify its public URL, then promote it separately.

faq.question: Does deployment run database migrations?
faq.answer: No. Deployments do not run migrations, seed data, or schema push. Run the project's approved database workflow separately.

faq.question: What deployment failures can it diagnose?
faq.answer: It checks build artifacts, authentication, branch scope, environment scope, runtime logs, public URLs, host binding, and deployed ports.
